normalizations: The api_server origin is recorded as `<mock>`; the localhost rewrite target as `127.0.0.1:<port>`. Neither the host nor the port is recorded.
notRecorded: NON-BUFFERING is not recorded: the peer answers one chunk, so a buffered reply cannot distinguish a piping route from a buffering one. The pinned property is source-derived (`from.body.pipe(to)` in src/util.js forwardFetchResponse) and the GO side is proved by an implementation test against a peer that writes a chunk and then BLOCKS. The `holdOpen` rule that would make it recordable lives on an unmerged lane branch and is deliberately NOT taken into this route lane.

the koboldcpp ABORT leg POSTs `{base}/api/extra/abort` on client close; the peer answers immediately, so there is no in-flight request to abandon. Labelled implementation test, pinned parity unobserved.

the Ollama replay of MULTIPLE frames: the peer delivers its body as ONE chunk, so `JSON.parse(partialData)` sees two concatenated objects and the frame loop emits nothing until end. The recorded scenario uses a single frame; multi-frame chunking is a peer property, not a route property.
